widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: What spare part number was consumed when resolving the mould shut-off gapping and particulate indentation on IM-780?

[maintenance_log] log_IM-780_02 - 2025-12-15 | Corrective Maintenance (IM780-FM-03) | Technician A. Deshmukh
Observed condition: Operators on Shift C noted excessive flash along the parting line of moulded housings. Verification of machine parameters confirmed clamp force was applied at the rated 180 ton limit. Inspection of the mould shut-off faces revealed minor particulate indentation and slight mechanical gapping under high tonnage loading.

Action taken: Cleaned parting lines thoroughly with approved solvent and non-abrasive brass scraper. Performed Prussian blue dye test to check mould face parallelism and contact distribution across the platens. Adjusted tonnage build-up profile on the machine controller to optimize clamping transition. Verified that mould change time parameters and shut-off alignment met plant standards.

Parts consumed: SP-3004. 

Downtime in minutes: 95 minutes. 

Technician remarks: Blue check verified uniform contact across parting surfaces. Flashing completely resolved on subsequent sample shots. Quality inspector signed off on component dimensions prior to releasing machine to production.

[manual] manual_PK-250 - Spare Parts Reference
Maintenance operations for the PK-250 Palletizing and Packaging Line rely on designated OEM replacement components to maintain system reliability. Part number SP-8001 designates the replacement gripper cups required to resolve vacuum retention failures during case picking. Part number SP-8002 designates the vacuum filter element scheduled for replacement at regular operational intervals to maintain optimal pneumatic suction. Part number SP-8003 designates the replacement PTFE tape used on the sealer bar assembly to prevent carton sticking and ensure consistent thermal sealing. All spare parts must be requisitioned through the Meridian Precision Works inventory system and stored in a dry, climate-controlled environment prior to installation.

[sop] sop_pm_hydraulic - Responsibilities
Plant Maintenance Engineers hold direct responsibility for scheduling and overseeing all hydraulic preventive maintenance activities during designated shift windows. Certified Maintenance Technicians execute lock-out/tag-out procedures, fluid sampling, filter replacements, and mechanical torque verifications. Production Supervisors ensure equipment is safely handed over to maintenance personnel and verify post-maintenance operational readiness before releasing machines back to active manufacturing schedules. The Quality Assurance department reviews maintenance sign-offs to ensure equipment operating parameters align with established production tolerances and safety standards.

sentences:
[sop] sop_conveyor_alignment - Records and Documentation
Upon successful completion of tracking and tension adjustment, the technician must record the asset identification (CV-120), date, shift designation (A, B, or C), pre- and post-adjustment tension values in Newtons, take-up bolt torque values, and technician employee ID on Maintenance Form MPW-MEC-F-014. Verify that cumulative operating hours are logged to track the 4000-hour gearbox oil change interval. The completed physical or digital record must be signed off by the Shift Supervisor and submitted to the plant maintenance database within the Chakan facility before the end of the active shift. [maintenance_log] log_CV-120_03 - 2026-05-14 | Corrective Maintenance | Technician A. Deshmukh
Unscheduled intervention performed during Shift B after production line stoppage triggered by drive unit slip. Observed condition: CV120-FM-02 failure mode identified. Drive pulley experienced significant slippage against the belt underside during heavy startup loading. Root cause determined to be localized wear on the rubber drive pulley lagging combined with reduction in frictional coefficient. Action taken: locked out power supply, removed worn ceramic-rubber lagging sections from 5.5 kW motorized drive drum, cleaned drum surface thoroughly, and installed replacement lagging material. Re-tensioned belt assembly to strict 3200 N tension requirement using hydraulic tensioning jacks. Consumed parts: SP-5002 (Drive Pulley Lagging Kit). Downtime incurred: 150 minutes. Technician remarks: Full-load torque test executed successfully with zero slippage observed at drive pulley interface.

[maintenance_log] log_AC-900_02 - 2025-10-05 | Scheduled PM | Technician R. Kulkarni
Observed condition: Routine 1000-hour preventive maintenance inspection conducted on AC-900 Rotary Screw Air Compressor during Shift A. Operating parameters recorded at 7.5 bar discharge pressure and 310 cfm free air delivery. Discharge temperature measured at 78 degC, well below the 95 degC limit. 

Action taken: Inspected intake valve, belt tension, and electrical connections. Cleaned external cabinet ventilation louvers. Checked fluid level of Synthetic PAO 46 compressor oil; level was optimal with no top-up required. Lubricated motor bearings per schedule. 

Parts consumed: SP-6001 (Air filter element replaced as a precautionary measure).

Downtime in minutes: 75 minutes.

Technician remarks: Compressor returned to service in Shift A. Unit operating smoothly with normal vibration and acoustic levels. Next scheduled service is at 2000 operational hours for air filter replacement per manual guidelines.

[manual] manual_LC-5500 - Overview
The LC-5500 Fiber Laser Cutting System, asset ID LC-5500, is manufactured by Photoniq Industrial and installed on 2023-04-18 within Line-5 Sheet Metal at Meridian Precision Works (MPW-PUN-01), located in the Chakan Industrial Area, Pune. This production asset operates continuously across three shifts: Shift A from 06:00 to 14:00, Shift B from 14:00 to 22:00, and Shift C from 22:00 to 06:00. The system is designed for high-precision industrial sheet metal fabrication, utilizing a solid-state fiber laser source coupled with a high-rigidity gantry motion system to process ferrous and non-ferrous sheet materials. Operators and maintenance personnel assigned to Line-5 must be trained on Photoniq Industrial operating procedures, adhere to MPW-PUN-01 facility safety protocols, and execute shift handover logs between Shifts A, B, and C to ensure uninterrupted, safe, and quality-compliant sheet metal manufacturing operations.

[sop] sop_compressor_service - Records and Documentation
The servicing technician must record all completed maintenance actions, operating hours, and part replacement serial numbers in the plant Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) logbook immediately upon task completion. The completed checklist must include the exact quantity of Synthetic PAO 46 oil added, final operating pressure (7.5 bar), and loaded discharge temperature readings. The signed physical work order and LOTO clearance certificate must be submitted to the maintenance office at the end of shifts A, B, or C. Records shall be archived for a minimum period of three years to support regulatory compliance audits and reliability trend analysis.

[sop] sop_spares_requisition - Records and Documentation
All executed Material Requisition Forms, electronic approval logs, and signed physical issue slips must be retained in the MPW-PUN-01 document control archive. Completed paper logs are archived by the Stores department for a minimum mandatory retention period of 36 months. Digital transaction records stored within the CMMS database must be backed up daily on the central MPW server located in the Pune facility server room, with an immutable audit trail preserved for financial compliance and annual inventory audits. Monthly consumption reports, discrepancy logs, and emergency issue records must be compiled by the Stores Supervisor and submitted to the Plant Operations Manager by the 5th working day of the following calendar month.

widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: What shielding gas proportion needs to be configured during the routine service on asset log_WR-3000_03 at the Chakan plant?
sentences:
[sop] sop_compressor_service - Procedure
1. Notify the control room, run the AC-900 compressor through a normal stop cycle, press the emergency stop, and isolate the main 415V electrical supply. Apply LOTO procedures to the isolator switch.
2. Isolate the unit from the main plant air header by closing the discharge isolation valve and slowly opening the manual condensate drain valve to vent internal system pressure to 0.0 bar.
3. Drain the compressor oil entirely by opening the sump drain valve while the system is warm. Collect and dispose of old fluid per environmental norms.
4. Replace the spent air filter element at its designated 2000-hour operational interval, ensuring the housing seal is clean and correctly seated.
5. Replace the spin-on oil filter and the air-oil separator element, adhering strictly to the 4000-hour change interval. Apply a light film of Synthetic PAO 46 to all rubber gaskets before hand-tightening plus an additional half-turn with a strap wrench.
6. Refill the compressor sump with fresh Synthetic PAO 46 oil up to the midpoint of the oil sight glass.
7. Remove LOTO devices, restore electrical power, open the discharge isolation valve, and start the compressor in unload mode. Check for leaks and verify that operating discharge pressure stabilizes at 7.5 bar.

[maintenance_log] log_WR-3000_03 - 2026-03-05 | Scheduled PM & Calibration | Technician R. Kulkarni
Observed condition: Routine 1000-hour preventive maintenance check due for WR-3000 Robotic Welding Cell at Chakan plant. Cell operates at 16 kg payload and 1520 mm reach with 0.05 mm repeatability. Axis-2 operating hours approached the 1000-hour axis grease interval. TCP drift noted within acceptable tolerance limits (+/- 0.12 mm).

Action taken: Performed complete mechanical inspection, cleaning of welding spatter from nozzle, and verification of shielding gas mix set to 82% Ar / 18% CO2. Applied high-temperature synthetic lubricant to Axis-2 per manufacturer specification. Re-ran Tool Center Point (TCP) calibration routine to correct minor drift. Verified wire feed rate steady at 9.5 m/min. Torch duty cycle maintained at 80%.

Parts consumed: SP-4004 (1 unit).

Downtime in minutes: 75 minutes (Shift A).

Technician remarks: Axis-2 mechanical binding check passed. Brake release functioning correctly. Cell returned to production queue without further issues.

[maintenance_log] log_WR-3000_02 - 2025-10-05 | Corrective Maintenance | Technician R. Kulkarni
Observed condition: During Shift B, visual inspection of structural bracket assemblies revealed severe porosity in the weld bead on part family W-402. Shielding gas mix verification at the regulator showed nominal delivery of 82% Ar / 18% CO2, but flow meter readings at the torch dropped to 10 L/min. Cause was traced to a fractured gas hose and partially blocked diffuser SP-4002. Action taken: Isolated cell, purged regulator, replaced damaged gas supply line, and installed a new diffuser SP-4002. Performed test welds verifying shielding gas flow restored to 17 L/min. Parts consumed: SP-4002 (Qty: 1). Downtime in minutes: 75. Technician remarks: Root cause linked to mechanical pinch point near the dress pack mount. Adjusted dress pack routing bracket to prevent recurrence. Operational parameters maintained at wire feed rate of 9.5 m/min and torch duty cycle of 80%.

widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: The LC-5500 is producing bad cuts with heavy dross on the bottom, which component should I replace?
sentences:
[maintenance_log] log_HP-450_01 - 2025-04-05 | Corrective Maintenance | Technician R. Kulkarni
Observed condition: Shift A operator reported audible pump cavitation and vibration during initial cold startup of asset HP-450. Reservoir temperature was recorded at 21 degC. Hydraulic system parameter checks indicated pump starvation on the suction side, corresponding to failure mode HP450-FM-04.

Action taken: Isolated system power and drained suction line. Inspected tank interior and found heavy contamination on the suction strainer. Removed and cleaned the suction strainer using solvent degreaser. Verified proper functioning of the reservoir immersion heater circuit. Replaced clogged line filter element with fresh SP-2004 stock. Refilled suction line, primed pump, and restarted system during Shift B.

Parts consumed: SP-2004 (1 ea)

Downtime: 45 minutes

Technician remarks: Cavitation noise eliminated upon restart. Oil tank heater maintained standby oil temperature above minimum threshold. Pump operation verified smooth with static reservoir fluid level normal at 380 L capacity. Plant location: MPW-PUN-01.

[maintenance_log] log_LC-5500_01 - 2025-04-22 | Corrective Maintenance | Technician A. Deshmukh
Unscheduled intervention during Shift B following operator report of poor cut quality. Inspection of the cut components revealed heavy dross on underside of cut edge, matching failure mode LC5500-FM-01. Further examination of the cutting head indicated nozzle orifice degradation and wear, which disrupted the gas flow dynamics for the assist gas types (Nitrogen and Oxygen). Action taken: Removed damaged nozzle and replaced with spare part SP-7001. Verified nozzle standoff_mm maintained at 0.8 mm relative to the sheet surface. Performed test cut on 10 mm mild steel, verifying gas pressure against the material parameter table. Total downtime: 45 minutes. Parts consumed: SP-7001 (1 unit). Technician remarks: Cut edge quality restored to acceptable manufacturing standards. No further dross observed.

[maintenance_log] log_LC-5500_03 - 2026-03-22 | Corrective Maintenance | Technician S. Deshmukh
Observed condition: Shift B operators reported poor cut quality during processing of 12 mm structural carbon steel sheet, well within the max_sheet_thickness_mm rating of 20 mm. Inspection of cut components revealed severe dross accumulation on the underside of the cut edge, corresponding to failure mode LC5500-FM-01. Edge geometry degraded due to inconsistent assist gas flow and orifice degradation.

Action taken: Powered down LC-5500 and locked out electrical supply. Removed inspection access cover on the cutting head assembly. Extracted worn cutting nozzle and cleaned seating surfaces with lint-free ethanol wipes. Installed replacement cutting nozzle part SP-7001. Performed nozzle centering routine and executed test cuts on reference material. Verified assist gas pressure alignment against standard cutting parameter table.

Parts consumed: SP-7001.

Downtime in minutes: 45.

Technician remarks: Worn nozzle orifice caused turbulent gas jet stream, leading to incomplete slag ejection. Post-repair test cuts showed clean edges free of dross. Handed over machine to Shift C production supervisor without further anomalies.
